findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. The `services` module will not compile, so the PR cannot be built or tested. The call needs `context.getUser()` as its argument, and the intended semantics should be rechecked.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which disables passkeys on the initial login
findings.body: The helper returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, passkeys were set up when the user was NOT yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`). Now `authenticate()` and `challenge(...)` call `fillContextForm` only if a user is already set, i.e. only during re-authentication. On a fresh login the user is null, so no WebAuthn challenge, RP id or conditional-UI attribute is rendered. Discoverable-key autologin and the external-key link then stop working. The existing tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and `passwordLoginWithExternalKey` would fail. The condition should cover both the user-null case and the re-authentication case, not replace one with the other.

findings.title: Re-authentication shows passkeys without checking that the user has a passkey
findings.body: During re-authentication passkeys are enabled whenever the realm has passkeys on and a user is set. The code never checks whether that user actually has a passwordless credential. A user with no passkey is therefore offered a conditional-UI/WebAuthn form that cannot succeed. The test comment for `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` says passkeys should not be shown for such a user. The test only turns passkeys off for the whole realm, so it does not exercise this case.

findings.title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators is inconsistent with the new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override
findings.body: The conditional-UI authenticator now returns false from `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`, so the allowed-authenticators bean is not set and IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is false. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` still returns `context.getUser() != null`, so SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS is true during re-authentication. The template is told to display authenticators that were never provided, which may render an empty list or fail on the missing attribute. Override it consistently as well. The new override also lacks `@Override`.

findings.title: Absence checks are written so they can never fail meaningfully
findings.body: The check calls `findElement(...)` inside `assertThat(..., nullValue())` and then `fail(...)`, all in a `try` block with `catch (Exception)`. `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is missing, which is the only path that passes. If the element exists, `assertThat(..., nullValue())` throws an AssertionError instead. The `fail` call is dead code. The check works only by accident and is hard to read. Use `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()` or `assertThrows`.
